title: The 10 Best Cordless Miter Saws
subtitle: Battery-powered miter saws from 6-1/2 to 12 inches, sliding and fixed, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: We ranked 10 cordless miter saws from Amazon's miter saw search results on rating, review volume, and five features: sliding rails, dual bevel, a brushless motor, a cut-line guide, and a battery in the box. Most name-brand saws are sold as bare tools for people who already own the batteries. Prices run from $149.95 for the RYOBI P553 to $1,139 for the Makita XSL06PT kit.

changelog.note: Prices, ratings and review counts re-checked on every listing. Biggest price moves: the DEWALT DCS361M1 rose from $329 to $379.99; the VEVOR J0XL-DU04-185 dropped from $236.90 to $201.36. Prices were captured during Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days sale, so some may be temporarily lower.
Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX 7-1/4-Inch Sliding Miter Saw, Tool Only (DCS361B)
products.verdict: The best-selling cordless miter saw on Amazon by a wide margin, with 3,087 ratings at 4.8 stars. A 7-1/4-inch slider for anyone already on DEWALT 20V batteries.
pros: 3,087 ratings at 4.8 stars, and 800+ bought in the past month
DEWALT rates it at about 183 cuts of 2x4 pine per charge
Cut-line system lights the blade path with nothing to calibrate
Cuts 3-5/8" nested crown and 3-1/2" base standing up
cons: Tool only: battery and charger cost extra
The listing's spec table calls the motor brushed
7-1/4" blade limits crosscut height compared with a 10" or 12" saw

products.name: DEWALT 20V MAX 7-1/4-Inch Sliding Miter Saw Kit with 4.0Ah Battery (DCS361M1)
products.verdict: The same DCS361 saw as the bare tool, packaged with a 4.0Ah battery and charger. For $32 more than the tool alone, it's the cheapest way into a name-brand cordless miter saw if you own no DEWALT packs.
pros: Battery (DCB204) and charger included, so it cuts out of the box
Only $32 more than the bare tool
11 positive miter stops on a stainless detent plate
Cut-line blade positioning for trim work
cons: One 4.0Ah pack: expect to stop and recharge on a full day of framing
The listing's spec table says brushless and 16 ounces; the DEWALT bullets and the bare-tool listing say otherwise, so ignore that table

products.verdict: A full-size 12-inch dual-bevel slider that runs on a single 20V MAX or FLEXVOLT battery. It cuts 14 inches wide and 6-1/2-inch base standing up, which covers almost everything a corded 12-inch saw does.
pros: 14" horizontal crosscut, 6-1/2" base and 6-1/2" nested crown
Takes any DEWALT 20V MAX or FLEXVOLT battery

Bevel pawls for quick 22.5° and 33.9° settings

51.7 lb tool only, heavy to carry between rooms

avoid.name: VEVOR Sliding Compound Miter Saw, 7-1/4 inch Blade, DC 18.5V Cordless, Battery and Charger Included, for Cutting Wood, Metals, Laminates
avoid.flag: Proprietary 18.5V battery of unstated size; sold for metal with a 24T blade
avoid.verdict: It's a best-seller and the cheapest complete kit in the search, but the battery fits nothing else, the listing never says how big it is, and it markets a 24-tooth wood blade for metal. The RYOBI PBT01B costs about the same and runs on a battery platform with hundreds of tools.
reasons: The spec table lists the battery as "Nonstandard" 18.5V. It doesn't fit any tool platform, and the listing never gives its amp-hour rating, so you can't estimate runtime or price a spare.
The title says it cuts metals, but it ships with a 24-tooth blade at 3,800 rpm. That's a coarse framing blade, not a metal-cutting setup.
The listing contradicts itself on bevel. One bullet says bevel and miter both adjust "up to ±45°"; the description says the bevel is 0-45° left only.
The spec table lists blade material as ADC12, a die-cast aluminum alloy used for housings, and no warranty term is stated beyond a customer-service request link.

buyers_guide.q: Is a cordless miter saw powerful enough?
buyers_guide.a: For trim, flooring, and most 2x framing, yes. DEWALT rates the 7-1/4" DCS361 at about 183 cuts of 2x4 pine per charge, and the 12" DCS785 cuts 14 inches wide. Where a cordless saw falls short is all-day production cutting on one or two batteries. If the saw lives on a bench next to an outlet, a corded saw costs less for the same capacity.

buyers_guide.q: Should I buy the kit or the bare tool?
buyers_guide.a: Buy the bare tool if you already own batteries on that platform. The saw is the expensive part, and a pack you already have works fine. If you're starting from zero, a kit like the DEWALT DCS361M1 adds a 4.0Ah battery and charger for $32 over the bare tool, which is less than buying them separately.

buyers_guide.q: What blade size do I need?
buyers_guide.a: 7-1/4" covers trim and 2x lumber, and the sliding versions crosscut a 2x10 or 2x12. A 10" or 12" saw cuts taller base molding and wider boards but weighs 34 to 52 pounds. A 6-1/2" saw like the Makita XSL05Z is a trim tool, sized for baseboard and casing.

A slider pulls the blade through the board, so a small blade crosscuts wide stock. The 7-1/4" RYOBI PBT01B crosscuts a 2x10, while the fixed 10" DEWALT DCS714 stops at 6 inches wide. Fixed saws are lighter and more compact, which is why trim carpenters like them.

More than any spec. A saw that runs on packs you already own saves the cost of batteries and a charger. Avoid saws with a proprietary battery that fits nothing else, like the VEVOR on this page: when that battery dies, you're shopping for a part that may not be sold separately.

A single-bevel saw tilts one way, so for the opposite bevel you flip the board. That's fine for framing. Dual bevel saves time on crown and long runs of matched trim. Here, the DEWALT DCS785 and DCS714 and the Makita XSL05Z and XSL06PT bevel both ways.
